title: A long edit with many zooms shows one Zoom lane per track, not one per zoomed clip
goal: On an edit where many clips are zoomed, the timeline stacks a separate, mostly empty Zoom row under the track for every zoomed clip, so the hour-long reference edit shows 126 of them and everything below is pushed out of sight. Show a track's zooms on as few rows as the zoom mock draws, so a long edit reads like a short one.
notes: Seen 2026-11-14 by the-timeline-of-an-hour-long-edit-scrolls-zooms: queue/audits/2026-11-14-timeline-hour-long-fit-sc.png shows three Zoom rows under V1 and more below the fold. Cause in code: Sources/Photonz/TimelineTrackRows.swift, TimelineTrackRow.lateBody, `if row.zoomedClips.contains(clip.layerID) { ZoomLane(layerID: clip.layerID, ...) }` inside the per-clip ForEach, so each zoomed clip gets a ZoomLane row (ZoomLane.swift). The reference edit (Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 60) carries 126 zooms. They did not show as a cost in a sample of a zoom (ZoomBarsView absent from the top frames), so this is about reading the timeline, not speed. Design question for the runner: one shared Zoom row per track (bars side by side, they never overlap in time on one track?) versus only the picked clip's rows; the mock draws a picked clip's Scale and Centre lanes.
acceptance: On the 60 minute reference edit the timeline shows no more Zoom rows under V1 than the zoom mock (video-zoom-wt.html) draws for a picked clip, and every zoom bar is still reachable and pickable
The zoom walks (pick-several-zooms-walk, zoom-bar-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk) stay green and a walk photographs the long edit's timeline with its zooms
Picking a clip still shows its zooms where the mock puts them

log.note: From the-timeline-of-an-hour-long-edit-scrolls-zooms pass 4 (2026-11-15): the 126 Zoom lanes DID cost speed on a scroll (about 9 ms of a 46 ms frame, each rebuilt every frame); fixed in c0e1a50b1 by culling against EditorState.timelineRowsSight. Whatever this task changes, a Zoom row must keep reading the window only when its zooms reach the rows' sight (docs/design/video.md 8f rule 9).

Adversarial pass: chose one shared Zoom row per track over showing only the picked clip's row, because a clip's zooms stay inside the clip and clips on a track sit side by side, so the bars never stack, and every zoom stays reachable without picking its clip first (the picked-only option would hide 125 of 126 zooms). Consequences handled: the label picks every zoom on the track (across clips, as a box already could), and Shift/Command click on a bar of another clip on the same row adds it to the pick instead of starting over, keeping the first clip in hand. zoomLaneRows stays keyed by clip (each zoomed clip on a track names the lane's row), so box picks, right clicks and walk lookups by 'Zoom <clip>' work unchanged; walks may also say 'Zoom <track>'.

Verified: new walk a-long-edit-has-one-zoom-lane-per-track-walk (60 min reference edit, no flags): '126 zooms on 126 clips share one Zoom lane under V1', a click on a bar picks it with its box up, Shift click on a bar of another clip adds it, the label picks all 126 (panel reads Mixed). 21 other zoom-touching walks run: 19 ok; clicking-a-timeline-item-moves-the-playhead-walk and a-transition-is-picked-at-the-cut-walk fail identically on plain main (stashed run), folded into walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-27. Scripts/test.sh green. Pictures looked at: whole hour (one Zoom row, Background and Music in sight), first minute (150% and 190% bars of two clips side by side), one picked (box on picture, panel Zoom 150%), two clips picked, all picked.

left rough: on the hour-long edit the panel takes ~1 s to show a picked zoom's rows (empty at 0.5 s); belongs to the-timeline-of-an-hour-long-edit-scrolls-zooms' speed work, not filed. At the whole-hour view zoom bars are faint 3 pt slivers; noted in the audit rough for the user.

One Zoom lane per track (ZoomLane takes the track's zoomed clips); the 60 min reference edit shows 1 Zoom row under V1, not 126. Label picks every zoom on the track, Shift click adds bars from other clips.
